questions.prompt: A Hydrilla shoot gave 6 bubbles per minute at a lamp 40 cm away, and 18 bubbles per minute at 20 cm. How many times faster was photosynthesis with the lamp closer?
Plan an investigation to find how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis in Hydrilla.
questions.modelAnswer: Place a Hydrilla shoot upside down in a test tube of water with a pinch of baking soda (for CO₂). Put a lamp at different distances (10, 20, 30, 40 cm). After letting it settle for 2 minutes at each distance, count the oxygen bubbles released in one minute. Keep the same shoot, water temperature (use a beaker of water as a heat shield), CO₂ level and lamp. Repeat each count three times and plot bubbles per minute against distance.
questions.explain: Criterion B: a classic fair test.

questions.prompt: Is each one an input (raw material) or an output (product) of photosynthesis?
